items.title: Build the id set of a repeated PromQL selector once per query
items.head: b56cfb0261aa
items.claim: A repeated one-series selector builds its id set once. Run 3 (confirm, head b56cfb0261aa on fd328d4baedf, 64-vCPU host, 16 pinned cores): 5.7-6.7 ms off each repeat (x + x 41.2 -> 34.8 ms, -15.5%; x + x + x 61.9 -> 48.4 ms, -21.8%; ~200-series y + y -11.7%); controls and the pk_range guard not slower.
items.pass_if: Confirm run on the rebased head: 05481 prints 1, 1, 2, 2 (only those four rows) on B and fails on A; the integration test passes; the repeated-selector queries of promql_repeated_selector.xml are significantly faster by at least 4 ms per repeat; no control or promql_selector_pk_range query is reported slower. If it passes, I mark it ready-to-submit with no further changes.
items.notes: 2026-11-04: run 2 passed on the numbers. The branch then conflicted with master (PrometheusHTTPProtocolAPI.cpp: master added StoragePrometheusQuery::applySettingsForPrometheusQuery), so I rebased onto fd328d4baedf and moved the cache setup into that helper. Review round 4 fix (b56cfb0): always install the non-waiting cache (a PromQL query inside a mutation kept the mutation's waiting cache before); 05481 pins use_index_for_in_with_subqueries = 1, use_query_condition_cache = 0. PR text is final except the setup line's base sha. gtests PreparedSetsCache.* need ENABLE_TESTS=ON (or upstream CI); running 05481 with random settings (flaky check) would be useful. Related upstream: 118801. 2026-11-05: run 3 passed; merges cleanly with master 39b9f2d5aedb; final review Approve (nit: spill_state not moved on adoption). Optional before submitting: an HTTP API test of x + x + x with use_index_for_in_with_subqueries=0&max_threads=1 (the no-wait path is otherwise covered only by the gtest); it would need another build. My recommendation: submit as is.

items.title: Grow the timeSeries*ToGrid bucket map before inserting a colliding key
items.head: e6d27f5cc1d46392c894e989a64266fc7cf20568
items.claim: Run 2: the gap slowdown goes away in time order (run 1: 8.8x / 6.5x), and the merge with the run after the gap first gets about 3x faster (probes as with the pre-#124773 1/2 limit). Contiguous, late-start, sparse-gap, every-2nd-minute and 4-samples-per-minute series are unchanged in time and memory.
items.pass_if: 05474 passes on A and B; gap LastToGrid and RateToGrid at least 3x faster; the later-run-first merge at least 2x faster; no guard query significantly slower (contiguous, late_start, gap_sparse, every_2nd, dense, bucketing, aggregation_functions); gap_sparse and every_2nd memory_usage within 5%.
items.notes: Run 2 (head e6d27f5cc1d4) failed its pass rule: T3 1.93x vs a 2x floor that was my mis-prediction, and 5 of 7 timeseries_to_grid_bucketing queries slower, most likely the part-layout draw of that file's fill (A/A on one master binary: medians 10% apart across fills). Gap T1/T2 8.4x/5.7x, aggregation_functions 21 of 35 faster, none slower. Review rounds 5-7 found three more shapes where the rule misfires (long-grid gaps; a sparse gap arriving later-run-first; jittered every-2nd-bucket series). Branch tip 84bdb18276cb is pushed but unbuilt, with two round-7 Majors open; `head` stays at the measured e6d27f5cc1d4. DECISION FOR JAMES (issue 10): (A, recommended) park this branch and treat upstream 124777 (dense array) as the fix for 125759; (B) one more iteration (8-cell run check, displaced-key fix), then a build and run 3 with the bucketing guard on byte-identical data copies. Closes upstream issue 125759. Related upstream: 124773 (caused it), 124777.

items.title: Stop evaluating an ALP parameter pair once it cannot beat the best one
items.head: d6f173c6e3d3228867a5815d441e561fc572a94a
items.claim: Run 2 (head d6f173c6e3d3): same bytes as master. In the encoder-alone harness under clang 20 at the release flags, Float64 decimal-like values take 38-93% less encode CPU, full-precision and random doubles 1-9% less, Float32 6-88% less; nothing is slower. End to end (prediction): small-block rtn about -45%, small-block rnd about -2%, codecs_float_insert ALP rows faster or unchanged.
items.pass_if: 05480 (4 pinned sizes) passes on A and B; 04612 and 05054 pass on B; codecs_float_alp_small_blocks rtn at least 30% faster and rnd not significantly slower; codecs_float_insert ALP rtn significantly faster, and no ALP row of codecs_float_insert slower than the slowest unchanged-codec row (NONE, LZ4, ZSTD, DoubleDelta, Gorilla, FPC) of the same run.
items.notes: Run 1 (d4c58e0009b4) failed: codecs_float_insert ALP mon +10.2%, seq +4.0%. Cause: clang vectorizes master's scoring loop; the per-value cut-off made it scalar, which loses where pairs are cut late (values that are not decimals). My harness used g++ and missed it. Fix 32eb990cdbb9 (cut-off only under RD_SIZE_THRESHOLD_LIMIT, each sample seeded with the previous best pair + 1); 05480 gained two pinned sizes (bd592b96a5d7, ded70dddecf1, d6f173c6e3d3) and a chassert. Price: the small-block rnd gain shrinks from -16% to about -2%. Run 1's A binary (c189bd99fbda) can be reused. If a debug build is at hand, run 05480 on it once (chassert). ALP is GA on master since 129732: enable_alp_codec is a no-op there, harmless in the test. Merges cleanly with master 2f701ba6d627. After a pass I add T1's end-to-end number to the changelog entry.
